title: Convex minimization with a fixed non-Euclidean proximal oracle
summary: A hidden finite convex objective is accessed only through the exact proximal point associated with a fixed power of an ell-p distance and a fixed positive coefficient.

description_paragraphs: Minimize an unknown finite convex function $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ globally and return a point with small objective gap.
task.formulation: Minimize an unknown finite convex function $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ globally and return a point with small objective gap.

description_paragraphs: Fix $2<p<s<\infty$ and $\lambda,R>0$. The class consists of finite convex functions having at least one attained global minimizer $x^\star$ with $\|x^\star\|_p\le R$. No uniform Lipschitz, smoothness, or objective-scale bound is imposed.
The localization ball is only a promise about one global minimizer. It does not restrict query centers or final outputs.

description_paragraphs: The only information interface is $$P_f(c)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^d}\{f(x)+\lambda\|x-c\|_p^s\},\qquad c\in\mathbb R^d.$$ One call returns this unique minimizer only, with no accompanying function value or subgradient.

The positive coefficient $\lambda$ and exponents $p,s$ are public and fixed for the entire interaction. The algorithm may choose the center but may not choose another regularization coefficient or power. Public inputs are $d,p,s,\lambda,R,\varepsilon$; the objective is hidden.
oracle.operation: The only information interface is $$P_f(c)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^d}\{f(x)+\lambda\|x-c\|_p^s\},\qquad c\in\mathbb R^d.$$ One call returns this unique minimizer only, with no accompanying function value or subgradient. The positive coefficient $\lambda$ and exponents $p,s$ are public and fixed for the entire interaction. The algorithm may choose the center but may not choose another regularization coefficient or power. Public inputs are $d,p,s,\lambda,R,\varepsilon$; the objective is hidden.

description_paragraphs: Return any measurable $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d$ determined by the transcript. It need not be a queried center or a proximal response.
output.feasibility: Return any measurable $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d$ determined by the transcript. It need not be a queried center or a proximal response.

description_paragraphs: The loss is $f(\widehat x)-f^\star$, where $f^\star=\min_{x\in\mathbb R^d}f(x)$.
metric.base_expression: The loss is $f(\widehat x)-f^\star$, where $f^\star=\min_{x\in\mathbb R^d}f(x)$.

description_paragraphs: One exact fixed-coefficient proximal reply costs one call. The total number of calls is bounded on every instance and every realization of the private seed. Exact internal computation, storage, and specification of arbitrary finite query centers are uncharged.
resource.budget: One exact fixed-coefficient proximal reply costs one call. The total number of calls is bounded on every instance and every realization of the private seed. Exact internal computation, storage, and specification of arbitrary finite query centers are uncharged.

components.description: Its accounting convention is stated in the resource paragraphs.

description_paragraphs: Queries, stopping decisions, and the output are measurable functions of the preceding transcript and an instance-independent private random seed. The unknown instance is fixed before the seed is realized. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.
Internal exact-real computation and storage using public inputs and received information are uncharged. The stated budget must hold on every execution path.
The guarantee is per fixed objective, with an independent private seed and a pathwise query cap.
The algorithm is deterministic and adaptive. Queries, stopping, and the output may use the complete preceding transcript. No span, support, zero-respecting, or memory restriction is imposed.
Internal exact-real computation and storage are uncharged. The stated budget holds on every admissible instance and every response history.
The error bound is deterministic for every admissible objective.

regimes.predicate_text: $2<p<s<\infty$, $\lambda,R,\varepsilon>0$, and $d\ge\lceil C_p(1+\kappa^{(p+3)/\rho})\rceil$. $d\ge\lceil(2+12\cdot64^p)(1+(\lambda R^s/\varepsilon)^{(p+3)/(s+s/p-1)})\rceil$. This is sufficient, not necessary. The lower construction is one finite distribution sampled before the algorithmic seed. The fixed coefficient is an essential part of the interface.
